title: Hamilton police investigate after witnesses report group shouting pro-Nazi comments at demonstration
summary: Hamilton police are investigating after receiving reports that a group of about 20 to 25 people dressed in black and wearing masks were shouting pro-Nazi comments at a downtown demonstration Saturday.

image.caption: Police are seeking information, photos and videos after receiving complaints about a weekend demonstration in downtown Hamilton, saying police 'take hate-motivated incidents seriously.' (Hamilton Police Service)

blocks.text: Hamilton

Hamilton police are investigating after receiving reports that a group of about 20 to 25 people dressed in black and wearing masks were shouting pro-Nazi comments at a downtown demonstration Saturday.
'Hate, racism and intimidation have no place in our community,' mayor-elect says

Hamilton police are investigating after receiving reports that a group of about 20 to 25 people dressed in black and wearing masks were shouting pro-Nazi comments at a downtown demonstration on the weekend.
The gathering took place shortly before 6 p.m. ET on Saturday at the corner of King and James streets, police said in a Saturday release.
Witnesses reported seeing participants carrying signs that displayed the words "white only," and hearing the group yell white nationalist and pro-Nazi comments, police said
Police said the group walked south through the Frank A. Cooke Transit Terminal on MacNab Street South before returning to vehicles and leaving the area.

blocks.text: "Hamilton police take hate-motivated incidents seriously and remain committed to addressing hate, supporting those impacted, and working alongside community partners to foster a safe and inclusive city," the release said.

Police encourage anyone who experienced or witnessed a hate-motivated crime or incident to report it to help investigators "identify patterns and better understand the experiences of affected communities." This includes incidents that "may not meet the threshold of a criminal offence."
Anyone with information, photos or video footage of Saturday's demonstration, or who witnessed potential criminal activity, is asked to contact Hamilton police.
'Get out of our city,' mayor says

An Instagram post from the Hamilton Anti-Racism Resource Centre (HARRC) shows a video that appears to be a demonstration of about 20 people covered all in black. Some are holding a sign that says "Whites First."
The video was shot at around 5:30 p.m. at the corner of King and James Streets on Saturday, according to centre.
In an email to CBC Hamilton, mayor-elect Keanin Loomis condemned the demonstration, calling it a "disgusting display of hate and white supremacy."
"You are not welcome in Hamilton. Get out of our city," Loomis said. "Hate, racism and intimidation have no place in our community."
He said he is in contact with Hamilton police Chief Frank Bergen as officers work to identify those responsible.
"Hamilton belongs to everyone," Loomis said. "We will not stand by while hate tries to find a home here."

blocks.text: Ward 2 Coun. Cameron Kroetsch said he has spoken with many residents concerned about what ongoing demonstrations by white supremacists in the ward.
"Everyone I know wants them to stop," Kroetsch said in an email to CBC Hamilton, adding that he and other downtown residents see the demonstrations as "disgusting."
He said the use of "white only" messaging is hate speech and said the frequency of such public gatherings is increasing.
Kroetsch said a motion he brought forward during the previous council term will help the city name and condemn such incidents. But he said stronger police action is needed to put a halt to them.
"Until police are willing to respond to this hate in our community, quickly and decisively, it will persist."
Kroetsch noted Saturday's demonstration took place across the street from a police station in Jackson Square and only a few blocks from the main downtown police station.
"We deserve better and I hope the new chief will make this a priority."
